prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols includes a catch (502) of a breech comprising two longitudinal rails (400, 401) that are attached to pistol body or to an inserted container at one end in a rotary way and at the other end they are connected with a bridge (402). One of the rails (400, 401) is provided with an internal projection (405) protruding into a space between the rails (400, 401). The mechanism further includes the breech provided with a feeding bridge (250) and a cartridge feeder (500) positioned under the internal projection (405) and configured to push, after feeding of the last cartridge, from below against the internal projection (405), thus tilting the breech catch (502) from its basic position upward to an upper position in which the breech leans with its feeding bridge (250) against an outer surface (408) of the bridge (402) of the catch (502) of the breech to lock the breech in the rear position.

outputs.L1: A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols includes a breech catch (502) comprising two longitudinal rails (400, 401), each rotatably attached at one end to the pistol body or to an inserted container and connected at the other end by a bridge (402). One of the rails (400, 401) includes an internal projection (405) extending into the space between the rails (400, 401). The mechanism further includes a breech provided with a feeding bridge (250) and a cartridge feeder (500) positioned beneath the internal projection (405). After feeding the last cartridge, the cartridge feeder (500) is configured to push upward against the internal projection (405), thereby tilting the breech catch (502) from its basic position to an upper position. In this upper position, the feeding bridge (250) of the breech bears against an outer surface (408) of the bridge (402) of the breech catch (502), thus locking the breech in the rear position.
outputs.L2: A breech-locking assembly for automatic and semi-automatic pistols has a breech catch (502) formed by two lengthwise rails (400, 401). At one end, the rails are pivotably mounted to the pistol body or to an inserted container; at the opposite end, they are joined by a bridge (402). At least one rail (400, 401) includes an inward-facing projection (405) that extends into the area between the rails. The assembly also includes a breech having a feeding bridge (250), as well as a cartridge feeder (500) located beneath the inward projection (405). Once the final cartridge has been fed, the feeder (500) presses upward against the projection (405), causing the breech catch (502) to pivot from its normal position into a raised position. In this raised position, the breech’s feeding bridge (250) rests against an outer surface (408) of the catch bridge (402), thereby retaining the breech in its rearward position.
outputs.L3:
The breech catch mechanism is intended for use in automatic and semi-automatic pistols. It consists of two longitudinal rails that are rotatably attached either directly to the pistol body or to a container inserted into the body. At their opposite ends, the rails are joined by a transverse bridge, forming a unified catch assembly.

One of the longitudinal rails incorporates an inward-facing projection that extends into the space between the two rails. After the final cartridge has been fed, the cartridge feeder moves upward and presses against this projection. This force causes the breech catch to pivot from its basic position into an upper locking position.

Once the catch reaches the upper position, the breech’s feeding bridge comes to rest against the outer surface of the catch bridge. This engagement prevents the breech from moving forward and locks it in its rear position, thereby indicating that the magazine is empty.
outputs.L4:
The breech catch mechanism is intended for use in automatic and semi-automatic pistols to retain the breech securely in its rearward position after the final cartridge has been fired or fed from the magazine. The mechanism comprises two longitudinal rails arranged on opposite sides of the pistol and mounted so that they can pivot. These rails are connected by a transverse bridge, thereby forming a unitary catch member capable of tilting between a lowered, inactive position and a raised, locking position.

An inwardly directed projection is provided on the catch member. After the last cartridge leaves the magazine, the cartridge feeder rises and engages this projection from below. The upward force exerted by the feeder pivots the longitudinal rails and raises the transverse bridge into the path of the returning breech. As the breech moves forward from its rearward position, its feeding bridge comes into contact with the raised bridge of the catch. This contact prevents further forward movement and locks the breech open.

Because the catch is supported by two connected longitudinal rails, the locking force is distributed across the mechanism rather than being concentrated at a single point. The arrangement therefore provides stable engagement with the breech and helps ensure that the breech remains reliably retained in its rear position until the catch is released.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style summary of an automatic or semi-automatic pistol breech catch involving two longitudinal rails, a bridge, an internal projection, and a cartridge feeder.
counterfactuals.output: A breech-catch assembly for an automatic or semi-automatic pistol comprises first and second longitudinal rails interconnected by a transverse bridge. The bridge includes an inwardly directed projection configured to cooperate with the pistol breech, while the rails engage and are actuated by a cartridge feeder. Upon depletion of cartridges, movement of the feeder displaces the assembly so that the internal projection retains the breech in an open position.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how the breech catch (502), rails (400, 401), projection (405), feeding bridge (250), and cartridge feeder (500) interact to hold the breech in its rear position.
counterfactuals.output:
The parts form a position-controlled latch for the breech:

- The **cartridge feeder (500)** moves along the two **rails (400, 401)**, which keep it aligned with the cartridge path.
- The feeder carries the **breech catch (502)**. When the breech travels rearward, it passes the catch; the catch then engages behind the breech and prevents it from moving forward again.
- The **projection (405)** on the rail cooperates with the **feeding bridge (250)** to control the feeder’s position and, consequently, whether the breech catch is raised into engagement.
- In the rear/feeding position, the bridge and projection hold or guide the cartridge feeder so that **catch 502 remains in the breech’s path**, locking the breech at the rear while a cartridge is presented.
- As the feeding mechanism completes its movement, the bridge moves relative to projection 405 and shifts or cams the feeder/catch out of engagement. The breech is then released to move forward.

Thus, the rails guide the feeder, the projection and feeding bridge determine its latch position, and the catch on the feeder physically retains the breech in its rear position.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract for a pistol mechanism in which the cartridge feeder lifts a pivoting breech catch after the final round, causing the breech to remain locked open.
counterfactuals.output: A pistol mechanism includes a pivoting breech catch configured to selectively engage and retain the breech in an open position. A cartridge feeder within the magazine moves upward as cartridges are discharged and, after feeding the final cartridge, acts on the breech catch to pivot the catch into an engagement position. Upon subsequent rearward movement of the breech, the catch engages the breech and prevents its return to the closed position, thereby providing an automatic indication that the magazine is empty. Reloading or manual actuation of the catch permits release of the breech for movement toward the closed position.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
